newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil down on increased spot supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil down on increased spot supplies.

text.p: Singapore oil products prices were weaker on Wednesday with gas oil under downward pressure on increased offers and expectations of reduced buying from India due to the closure of two jetties at Kandla, traders said.

Gas oil was offered down by a Singapore trader who lowered its offer to as low as $29.90 for Nov 17-21 lifting fob, with buying interest heard at $29.70. Swaps also dipped to trade for November between $29.95 and $30.05, down from Tuesday's $30.20.
Traders said India might be forced to lower its December gas oil imports due to the increased port congestion at Kandla, on the Indian west coast, as a result of the jetty closures.
The jetties were damaged when two tankers carrying diesel collided. It was not clear when the jetties would be reopened and some traders estimate that it might take more than a month.
The Kandla port now has 18 tankers waiting to discharge. The Indian tender for December arrival cargoes closes on October 24.
Traders said jet fuel was offered down to $29.90 for mid-November lifting fob, with an early-November cargo offered at $30.00 but no bids were seen against it.
They said more than five million barrels of jet fuel are in storage in China, Guam, Singapore and the Middle East.

The buyer for 50,000-150,000 barrels of 97-octane unleaded, lowered his bid by just five cents from Tuesday, to $26.25 a barrel for November 16-21 lifting, fob Singapore. But the only offer was for 92-octane cargoes for November 18-22 at $24.90.
Naphtha fell with November paper lower from Tuesday by 20 cents at $22.50/ $22.70.
Fuel oil fell on strong selling by a major who offered a cargo for loading in early November at $118 a tonne.
Traders said the market is still long and Chinese buyers remained sidelined expecting prices pick up.
